newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, Feb 17 - Vancouver, BC - GRAIN - 4 Vessels loading, 30 waiting, delays of approx. 4 weeks. The wheat board has advised that they will not accept any new nominations until end-March/early April. Roberts Bank - COAL - 2 Vessels loading, 2 waiting, 9 due by end of Feb. Prince Rupert - GRAIN - 1 Vessel loading, 13 waiting, delays of approx. 4 weeks. Halifax, NS - Port ice free. No congestion. Halifax shipyards and Dartmouth yard available for ship repairs.

HONDURAS, Feb 17 - Puerto Cortes - Four vessels berthed of which 1 discharging/loading containers/generals, 2 loading bananas, 1 discharging gasoline, 1 vessel anchored in ballast. 11 Vessels due of which 1 passenger. 7 To discharge/load containers/generals, 2 to load bananas, no berthing delays expected. Only one of the three tug boats are working well, one tug boat out of order for one year and one tugboat working with one engine only.

MEXICO, Feb 18 - Tampico - Vessels in port, 2 general cargo, 3 mineral, 1 scrap, 1 coke, 1 steel coils, working normally. Altamira - Vessels in port, 1 wood, 1 steel coils, 2 chemicals, 1 repair, working normally. Veracruz - Vessels in port, 2 sugar, 1 iron, 3 containers, 3 grain, 1 repair, 3 general cargo, working normally. Manzanillo - Vessels in port, 1 cars, 1 fruit, 1 scrap, 1 steel coils, 2 general cargo, 1 chemical, 2 containers, working normally. Coatzacoalcos - Vessels in port, 9 chemicals, 7 oil tankers, 1 repair, working normally.

PANAMA, Feb 17 - Balboa - Vessels operating, 1 general, 1 motor vehicles. Cristobal - Vessels operating, 1 bulker, 1 container, 1 general, 1 lpg. Panama Canal - Working to full capacity. Transit booking system working normally. 37 Vessels due, 34 in queue, 15 booked, 42 scheduled.

UNITED STATES, Feb 17 - Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating, 6 bulkers, 3 container vessels, 1 ro-ro, 1 auto vessel, 1 tanker, 3 general cargo, 1 cable vessel on standby, 3 vessels in repair yard, 3 bulkers awaiting berth of which 2 to discharge sugar. Honolulu, HI - Harbour - 2 Container vessels alongside, 3 tugs and barges alongsi. Barbers Point - 1 Tug and barge alongside. Offport moorings - 2 Tankers discharging crude.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - No congestion expected at Dundalk terminal this week. Clear Candd canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working normally with no delays. Consol Coal - 3 Days average waiting time. Liquid bulk facilities working normally with no berthing congestion. Anchorages vacant at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - Work continues at Columbus Strt terminal to Piers Fenders. Routine maintenance work at north Charleston terminal, but no delays expected. Jacksonville, FL - No berthing congestion at Jacksonville or Fernandina Beach, FL.

New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, container or tanker terminals. Congestion at sugar terminal. Norfolk, VA - Southern Coal pier - 11 Vessels due during the week, 2 anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal - 7 Vessels due. Pier IX Coal terminal - 4 Vessels due. Cargill - 1 Vessel due during the week. Container and general cargo terminals working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals all working normally. All channels ice free, with prevailing depths available. Scheduled maintenance to Southern Coal pier no. 1 ship loading system from 8-29 april. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion at Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington. Savannah, GA - Garden city terminals expecting moderate week except for Saturday where 8 vessels currently due. Ocean terminal - Slow week expected with no more than 2 vessels working on any day.

EAST COAST - Moderate week with no delays expected. Colonial Marine terminals bulk clay facility expects long delays. All liquid bulk facilities working normally with no congestion expected. Navigation normal. GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, Cargill grain elevator, public elevator or farmland grain elevator. Congestion at some oil/chemical docks. Mobile, AL - No congestion expected 16-27/2. New Orleans, LA - Seasonal rains causing some delays, especially for grain loading. Grain shipments normal for the season. River stage at 12.7 ft. and expected to go up to 13.0 ft. by 17/2 and down to 12.2 ft. by 23/2. Normal transit times can be expected. Draft for Mississippi river gulf outlet is 36 ft. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 47 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt and 46 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - At present there are 14 grain vessels in port of which 4 loading, 9 waiting. Average waiting period is 3-5 days. Coos Bay, OR - Port working normally. One log vessel due by end of the month. Activity at Glenbrook nickel berth due to increase with 1 vessel discharging this coming week. Linerboard shipment due next week at Coos Bay dock. Channel deepening project expected to be halted next week until 1 July. Sediment has been dredged from upper shipping channel and 35 ft. depth retained. Honolulu, HI - Traffic light for coming week, with no delays expected for offport anchorages or inport berths. Slight delays may occur due to naval open house on 14/2 and 17/2.

Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan (lb-212-214) - Moderately busy for Feb, with delays of 1-2 days at anchor for vessels currently awaiting berths. Koch Carbon (lb-211) - 4 Vessels due for Feb, no delays expected. Kaiser (la-49) - Moderately busy for Feb, with 2-3 days delay expected for vessels awaiting berths (coal,petcoke). Feb looks moderately busy in Los Angeles, Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes.
